deep.reconstruction:
Context. This bundle holds Riemann's lecture on the equilibrium of electricity on three parallel circular cylinders. In 2D this is a Dirichlet problem: find an analytic function on the region outside three circles whose real part takes given values on the circles. The previous page introduces an auxiliary function that is real on the three peripheries, has three simple poles, and is otherwise continuous. It notes that this function takes each real value only three times and starts counting values with the argument principle, ∫ d log(ζ − a) over the boundary.

This page names that function 𝔷 ('zur Abkürzung') and inverts the viewpoint: z, the point of the circle region, is now treated as a function of 𝔷.

(1) Sketch. A horizontal line with marked points α, β, γ, i.e. the real 𝔷-axis, the image of the three circles. A later line reads roughly 'η(or z)=∞ : 𝔷=α, 𝔷=β, 𝔷=γ': three distinguished real 𝔷-values where some function becomes infinite.

(2) 'z als Function von 𝔷 stetig'. To study the inverse one must examine ∂z/∂𝔷, i.e. where it vanishes or becomes infinite. These are the branch points, the zeros of d𝔷/dz.

(3) Counting values. ∫ d log(𝔷 − a + bi) and ∫ d log(𝔷 − a − bi) are taken over the whole boundary. By the argument principle each is 2πi·(zeros − poles inside). The margin of the next page gives the values 0 and 6πi; the previous page has ±3πi. The intended conclusion (my reading) is that 𝔷 omits one half-plane and covers the other three times. So the region is a 3-sheeted branched cover of a half-plane, and the circles cover the real axis three times.

A consistency check of my own: Riemann–Hurwitz for the bordered region gives χ = −1 = 3·1 − B, so B = 4 simple branch points inside. On the doubled (Schottky) surface, of genus 2, this matches 2g − 2 = 2 = 3·(−2) + 8.

(4) Table '𝔷 | z1, z2, z3'. Each 𝔷 has three preimages z1, z2, z3. Riemann forms
- the power sums Σ z_i, Σ η_i z_i, Σ η_i² z_i, where η is an auxiliary function with values η_i at the three preimages;
- the cubic (η−η1)(η−η2)(η−η3) = 0.
The coefficients of the cubic, and the three sums, are symmetric, hence single-valued in 𝔷. He concludes ('folglich') that they are rational expressions in 𝔷 (third degree).

This is the standard Riemann device from the Abelian-functions theory. Given S_k = Σ η_i^k z_i for k = 0, 1, 2, a Vandermonde/Lagrange solve gives z_j = (S2 − (η_k+η_l)S1 + η_kη_l S0)/((η_j−η_k)(η_j−η_l)). So z is rational in η and 𝔷, with η algebraic of degree 3 over C(𝔷), and the surface is described as a trigonal algebraic curve.

(5) Bottom line: Σ c_n ((𝔷−a−bi)/(𝔷−a+bi))^n and ∫_0^∞ f(λ) e^{iλ𝔷} dλ. These are two ways to represent a function holomorphic in a half-plane:
- a power series in the Cayley-transformed variable w = (𝔷−(a+bi))/(𝔷−(a−bi)), with |w| < 1 when 𝔷 and a+bi lie on the same side;
- a Fourier–Laplace integral, which converges for Im 𝔷 > 0.
Both serve to solve the reduced Dirichlet problem on the half-plane.

(6) Right margin, cut off. It shows Z, ∂z/∂𝔷, 1/sqrt(∂Z/∂𝔷), Z/sqrt(∂Z/∂𝔷). This anticipates the next page. There, reflection in a circle (center p, radius r) gives (Z−p)/r = r/(Z'−p'), so the continuations of Z are Möbius images (aZ+b)/(cZ+d). Hence 1/sqrt(Z') and Z/sqrt(Z') transform linearly, with factor 1/sqrt(ad−bc). They are therefore two solutions of a second-order linear ODE in 𝔷, y'' + ½{Z,𝔷} y = 0.
errors: Step (4) as written is not justified for symmetric functions of z itself. Single-valuedness in the upper 𝔷-half-plane does not give rationality without continuation across the real axis. Across the axis, z continues by reflection in the circles, z ↦ p + r²/(z̄ − p̄), not by complex conjugation. So Σ z_i need not satisfy f(𝔷̄) = conj f(𝔷) and need not extend to a rational function. Rationality holds for functions real on the boundary (e.g. functions of 𝔷 and of a real-on-boundary η). This gap is plausibly why the next page switches to Möbius-covariant combinations, 1/sqrt(Z') and Z/sqrt(Z').

The recorded argument-principle values (0 and 6πi on the next page's margin) do not fit a simple count 'zeros minus 3 poles' if the poles are interior. They fit if the three poles lie on the boundary and are handled by indentation (the ±3πi on the previous page). As written, the bookkeeping is incomplete or ambiguous.
'rationale Ausdrücke dritten Grades' is unexplained. The degree claim is not derived on the page.

results.what: Exterior of three circles represented as a 3-sheeted branched cover of a half-plane via a function real on the circles; branch points located by zeros of the derivative; values counted by the argument principle
results.modern_name: Conformal mapping of a triply connected circle domain; Schottky double / real trigonal curve; Riemann–Hurwitz count
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (lectures and Nachlass), later Schottky 1877 and Schwarz

results.what: Symmetric functions of the sheet values are single-valued, hence rational; Lagrange/Vandermonde solution expresses the coordinate rationally in an auxiliary function and the base variable
results.modern_name: Primitive element / function field of an algebraic curve as a finite extension of C(𝔷)

results.what: Half-plane function representations: power series in the Cayley transform and Fourier–Laplace integral
results.modern_name: Cayley transform expansion; Paley–Wiener-type Fourier–Laplace representation

results.what: (Margin, developed next page) 1/sqrt(Z') and Z/sqrt(Z') transform linearly under Möbius maps, so they solve a 2nd-order linear ODE
results.modern_name: Schwarzian derivative method for circular-arc polygon maps

deep.surprise_reason: This material belongs to Riemann's known fragment on 'Gleichgewicht der Electricität auf Cylindern mit kreisförmigem Querschnitt und parallelen Axen / Conforme Abbildung von durch Kreise begrenzten Figuren', edited in the Werke/Nachträge. The page is a working sketch of methods already attributed to him. Notable details: the explicit 3-sheeted half-plane cover of a triply connected domain and the half-plane representations. Nothing here overturns standard attributions.

checkable.asserts: |w|^2 = ((x-a)^2+(y-b)^2)/((x-a)^2+(y+b)^2), so |w|<1 iff y and b have the same sign: the Cayley transform maps the half-plane containing a+bi to the unit disc
Derivative of a Möbius image: (aZ+b)'=(ad-bc)Z'/(cZ+d)^2 (letters renamed)
Lagrange/Vandermonde inversion recovers z1 from the three weighted sums
1/sqrt(Z') solves y''+(1/2){Z,t}y=0 (Schwarzian ODE); the same holds for Z/sqrt(Z')
Riemann–Hurwitz: a 3-sheeted cover of a half-plane by a triply connected region needs B=4 interior simple branch points
